questions.question: Moving water can do work in turning a turbine for generating electricity. This is an example of which energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1 **i.e. __**Kinetic energy.**__

**Explanation:**

 
• Every object around us which is moving possesses** kinetic energy.**
 
• In other words, every object around us **that has speed in it**, possesses **kinetic energy.**
 
• When a moving body is brought to rest (stopped) by an **opposing force**, the **kinetic energy is lost**, being used up to do work in overcoming the resistance of opposing force.

**Energy:**

 
• The** amount of energy** possessed by a body is equal to the **amount of work** it can do when its energy is released.
 
• A body that possesses energy can **exert a force **on another object.
 
• During this process, some of the energy of the bodies** transferred to the object.**
 
• By** gaining energy,** the object moves, and when the object moves, **work is said to be done. **
 
• It is a** scalar quantity.** It has only magnitude but no direction.
 
• The SI unit is **Joule** which is denoted by **J**.
 
• The energy required to do **1 Joule of work** is called **1 Joule energy**.
 
• The unit of energy is **Joule** and it is named after the **British physicist James Prescott Joule.**
 
• Joule is a small unit of energy, Sometimes, **'kJ'** is used as a bigger unit.
 
• The symbol of** kiloJoule is kJ. **
 
 
• **1 kJ = 1000 Joule**
 
 

**Kinetic energy:**

 
• The kinetic energy of a moving body is measured by the **amount of work** it can do before coming to rest.

 
 
• **Kinetic energy = 1/2×mv****2 ** 
 
• Where **m** = mass of the body,** v** = velocity of the body
 
 
 
• From the above formula, it is clear that:
 
 
• The kinetic energy of a body is **directly proportional **to the **mass of the body.**
 
• The kinetic energy of a body is **directly proportional **to the **square of the velocity of the body.**

questions.question: What is another name for involuntary muscle?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__ 

Muscle and its types:

__
 
• Muscles are groups of fiber made of cells that are protected by protective tissue.
 
• Types of muscles:

 
• Skeletal muscle or voluntary muscle.
 
• Smooth muscle or involuntary muscle.
 
• Cardiac muscle.

Explanation:__

**Involuntary muscle:**

__
 
• These are also **called smooth muscles.**
 
• These muscles are **non-striated.**
 
• These are muscles in the human body whose contraction is controlled by the **autonomic nervous system.**
 
• **Involuntary muscles** include all muscles whose activity is independent and not affected by voluntary nerve activity.

**Thus, non-striated muscle is another name for involuntary muscle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****Skeletal muscle:**

 
• It is also called** voluntary muscle.**
 
• A voluntary muscle is a **muscle that you choose to move, like those in the arms and legs, as opposed to the ones that move automatically, like the heart.**
 
• Muscle is the tissue in animals that produces movement or motion.
 
• **Voluntary **means have been done out of free will or by choice.

questions.question: While standing on Earth, suppose your weight has a value of 100 Newtons. If the Earth shrinks to half its diameter without any change in mass, then your new weight on the surface of the shrunken Earth, in Newtons, is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**400.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Weight of the body (W1) = mg;
 
• The surface of the earth with radius R. (Given 100 Newtons)
 
• Acceleration due to gravity on earth (g) = G.M/R²,
 
 
• G is gravitation constant, (M) is mass of earth and R is the initial radius of the earth.
 
 
 
• Now Final radius =R/2;
 
• New acceleration due to gravity on earth (g2) = (G.M)/(R/2)² = 4(G.M/R²) = 4g
 
• So new weight of Body (W2) = m. g2 = 4(m.g) [as mass of body is constant]
 
• **From above,**
 
 
• **W2 = 4* W1 =4*100 = 400 Newtons**. **Hence option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: What is the change in Electronegativity when we move from top to bottom in the Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Electronegative elements: 

 
• They have a high tendency of attraction towards electrons in a bond.
 
• These elements like F, Cl, S have one or two electrons short of achieving their octet in the outermost shell.
 
• Thus, they gain one or two electrons to fulfill their octet.
 
• Their electron affinity is high and they also have high ionization values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/432e7746affc2b0498998c5a944d6c1db716fa405183eb9609f75b50b635713e.png] 

 

 
• Electronegativity is defined as the tendency of an atom to attract a shared electron pair towards itself in a covalent bond.
 
• Electronegativity increases while moving across a period and decreases down a group.
 
• As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic radius decreases as a result of which the electronegativity increases.
 
• The increase in the size of atoms decreases the electronegativity of the elements as we move down the group.
 
• So, when we move from top to bottom in the Periodic Table Electronegativity decreases.

questions.question: This chemical equation "2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO + Heat" belongs to Which of the following type of chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option [3] i.e.__ **Combustion reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__** 

 
• Types of Chemical Reactions-The The basis for different types of reactions is the product formed, the changes that occur, the reactants involved, and so on. Different types of reactions are

 
 
• Combustion reaction
 
• Decomposition reaction
 
• Neutralization reaction
 
• Precipitation or Double-Displacement Reaction
 
 
 
• Combustion Reaction-
 
 
• It is a reaction with a combustible material with an oxidizer to give an oxidized product.
 
• An oxidizer is a chemical a fuel requires to burn, generally oxygen.
 
• An example of the combustion of magnesium metal.
 
 

2Mg + O2→2MgO + Heat 

Here, 2 magnesium atoms react with a molecule of oxygen-producing 2 molecules of the compound magnesium oxide-releasing some heat in the process.

 
• Decomposition Reaction-

 
 
• It is a reaction in which a single component breaks down into multiple products.
 
• Certain changes in energy in the environment have to be made like heat, light, or electricity breaking bonds of the compound. for example of the decomposition of calcium carbonate gives out CaO (Quick Lime) which is a major component of cement. 
 
 

​CaCO3(s)→CaO(s)+CO2(g) 

Here, the compound Calcium carbonate when heated breaks down into Calcium Oxide and Carbon Dioxide.

 
• Neutralization Reaction-

 
 
• It is basically the reaction between an acid and a base giving salt and water as the products.
 
• The water molecule formed is by the combination of OH- ions and H+ ions. The overall pH of the products when a strong acid and a strong base undergo a neutralization reaction will be 7.
 
• Consider the example of the neutralization reaction between Hydrochloric acid and Sodium Hydroxide giving out sodium chloride(Common Salt) and water.
 
 

 HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O 

Here, an acid and a base, Hydrochloric acid, and Sodium Hydroxide react in a neutralization reaction to produce Sodium Chloride(Common Salt) and Water as the by-products.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to reproduction in plants?

1. In asexual reproduction plants produce seeds identical to the parent.

2. In sexual reproduction parents and progeny have the same genetic makeup.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Reproduction in Plants:**

 
• The **production of new individuals from their parents** is known as Reproduction.
 
• There are **different modes of reproduction** in plants:
 
 
• Asexual Reproduction
 
• Sexual Reproduction
 
 

**Asexual Reproduction:**

 
• In asexual reproduction, new plants are obtained **without the production of seeds. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The new plants are **exact copies of the parent plant,** as they are produced from a** single parent.**
 
• It **does not include the fusion **of male and female gametes.
 
• It results in **offspring that are genetically identical** to their parents.
 
• **Examples: **
 
 
• **​**Budding, Fragmentation, Vegetative Propagation.
 
 

**Sexual Reproduction:**

 
• In sexual reproduction,** new plants are obtained from seeds.**
 
• Sexual reproduction** necessitates the genetic material of two parents.**
 
• Male and female sex cells, **known as gametes, **exist in parent plants.
 
• The **genetic material from the male and female gametes mixes **is referred to as **fertilisation**.
 
• As a result, neither of the parents and offspring are genetically similar. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Seeds** are the result of sexual reproduction.
 
• **Pollination** is the process through which flowering plants **reproduce sexually.**

questions.question:
Match the Chemical Effects of Electric Current with their descriptions:

 
 

 **Chemical effects of electric current**
 **Descriptions**
 
 

 a) Electrolysis
 1) oxidation during electrolysis
 
 

 b) Electroplating
 2) chemical process
 
 

 c) Cathode
 3) a thin layer of metal
 
 

 d) Anode
 4) reduction during electrolysis
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1:** **(a) - 2, (b) - 3, (c) - 4, (d) - 1**

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **Electrolysis: **Electrolysis is a chemical process that uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction. During electrolysis, positive ions migrate toward the negative electrode (cathode) while negative ions migrate towards the positive electrode (anode), where they undergo reduction and oxidation reactions respectively.
 
• ** Electroplating:** Electroplating is a process of depositing a thin layer of metal onto a conductive surface using electrolysis. It involves immersing the object to be plated (the substrate) and a metal electrode (the anode) into an electrolyte solution containing ions of the plating metal. 
 
• **Cathode**: In an electrolytic cell or electrochemical reaction, the cathode is the electrode where reduction (gain of electrons) occurs. It is the negatively charged electrode connected to the positive terminal of the power supply. During electrolysis, positively charged ions migrate toward the cathode, where they gain electrons and are reduced to form neutral atoms or molecules.
 
• **Anode**: In an electrolytic cell or electrochemical reaction, the anode is the electrode where oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs. It is the positively charged electrode connected to the negative terminal of the power supply. During electrolysis, negatively charged ions migrate toward the anode, where they lose electrons and are oxidized to form neutral atoms or molecules.

**Therefore, option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: Biodiversity is pivotal for maintaining ecosystem stability and providing essential services such as food, fiber, and natural medicines. What role does genetic diversity play within species in helping ecosystems respond to environmental changes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Improves adaptability to climate change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Genetic diversity within species increases the chances of survival during environmental changes by providing a wide range of traits that can help in adaptation.
 
• It allows species to evolve over time in response to changes in the environment, such as climate change, by ensuring that some individuals within the species carry traits that are better suited to the new conditions.
 
• High genetic diversity within a species reduces the risk of extinction because it increases the likelihood that some individuals will survive and reproduce under changing conditions.
 
• Genetic diversity contributes to the resilience of ecosystems by maintaining ecosystem functions and services, even as individual species face environmental stressors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodiversity**

 
 
• Biodiversity refers to the variety of life on Earth, including the variety of species, their genetic diversity, and the ecosystems they form.
 
• It is crucial for ecosystem stability, resilience, and the provision of ecosystem services such as food, clean water, and medicine.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Diversity**
 
 
• Genetic diversity is the variation in genes within a particular species. It includes the differences in DNA sequences between individuals within a species.
 
• High genetic diversity ensures that species can adapt to changes in the environment, resist diseases, and maintain healthy populations.
 
 
 
• **Ecosystem Services**
 
 
• Ecosystem services are the benefits that humans obtain from ecosystems, including provisioning services (food, water, fiber), regulating services (climate regulation, pest control), supporting services (nutrient cycling, soil formation), and cultural services (recreational, spiritual).
 
• Maintaining biodiversity is essential for sustaining these services.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change**
 
 
• Climate change refers to long-term changes in temperature, precipitation, and other atmospheric conditions on Earth.
 
• It is driven by natural processes and human activities, particularly the emission of greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide.
 
• Adaptation to climate change involves adjustments in natural or human systems to minimize damage and take advantage of opportunities created by changing climate conditions.

questions.question: When a ball is thrown upwards, then at what position will it's potential energy be maximum?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 4**__ i.e __**At topmost position**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When an object (ball) is thrown upwards its** velocity will decrease** as it goes upward due to deceleration by gravity.
 
• So its kinetic energy will decrease as it moves upward. But its potential energy will increase as it moves upward.
 
• **Kinetic energy** is zero and **potential energy is maximum** when the object reaches the topmost point.
 
• **Kinetic energy is maximum just before striking the ground.**

questions.question: Which organelle in an animal cell has the function of digesting larger extracellular and intracellular particles and autolysis?
questions.solution:
**Lysosomes are the cell organelles that are responsible for digesting larger extracellular and intracellular particles and autolysis.**

__**Explanation:**__

**Lysosomes - **

__
 
• These are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
 
• Lysosomes have several hydrolytic enzymes like **lipases**, **proteases**, **carbohydrases**, etc.
 
• With the help of these enzymes, **lysosomes digest all the extracellular & intracellular particles.**
 
• Lysosome keeps the cell clean by digesting any foreign material as well as worn-out cell organelles.
 
• They even digest themselves** (autolysis)** when they get injured by the process of **apoptosis **(Programmed cell death).
 
• For their phagocytic activities, they are also called the** ''suicidal bags''.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosomes **are the site for protein synthesis so they are also called the ''protein factory'' of the cell.
 
• **Peroxisomes**: It is a microbody. In-plant it helps in photorespiration. In animals concerned with peroxide metabolism.
 
• **Glyoxysome**: These are the special type of peroxisomes found in plants & some fungi.

questions.question: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium present in the soil at any given time, is referred as :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4**.

**Solution**

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Organisms need a steady supply of nutrients** to grow, reproduce, and regulate different functions. 
 
• **Nutrient cycling** is the **movement of nutrients through various components of the ecosystem**.

**Explanation:__**

__
 
• The **amount of nutrients like nitrogen, carbon, phosphorous, and calcium** present **in the soil at any given time is called the standing state **of the soil.
 
• **Nutrient cycles are of two types**:
 
 
• **Gaseous cycle**: The **reservoir is the atmosphere** for the gaseous cycle. An example of the gaseous cycle is the **nitrogen cycle and the carbon cycle.**
 
• **Sedimentary cycle: **The **reservoir is the Earth's crust** for the sedimentary cycle. An example of the sedimentary cycle is the **sulfur cycle and the phosphorous cycle.**
 
 

So, the **correct answer is option 4.**

**Additional Information:**__

 
• **Standing crop**: At each trophic level a **certain mass of living material is present at any given time**; this living mass is called the standing crop. It is **measured as the mass of living organisms or the number per unit area.**
 
• **Climax community**: A** community that is in equilibrium with the environment **is called a** climax community**. All **communities change (in composition and structure) with the environmental conditions**. This **change is ordered, sequential, and in parallel with the physical environment.**
 
• **Climax: **It is the **final stage of biotic succession** attained **by the plant community** in an area, in the present environmental conditions, at the present time.

questions.question: Why do soap solution bubbles appear coloured?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interference**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When light shines onto a bubble it seems to change colour.
 
• Not like those seen during a rainbow, that arises from differential refraction, the colours are seen during a soap bubble that arises from** interference of light reflecting off the front and back surfaces of the thin film**.

 
• **Interference** is a natural phenomenon that happens at every place and at every moment. 

 
 
• Interference is the phenomenon in which two waves superpose to form the resultant wave of the lower, higher, or same amplitude. 
 
• The most commonly seen interference is **optical interference or ****light interference**. 
 
• This is because light waves are randomly generated every which way by most sources. 
 
• This means that light waves coming out of a source do not have a constant amplitude, frequency, or phase.
 
• The most common example of interference of light is the soap bubble which reflects wide colours when illuminated by a light source.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scattering**, in physics, is a change in the direction of motion of a particle because of a collision with another particle. 
 
• In optics, **dispersion **is the phenomenon in which the phase velocity of a wave depends on its frequency. 
 
• **Polarization** is a property applying to transverse waves that specify the geometrical orientation of the oscillations.

questions.question: The movement of molecules of a dispersed phase in a zig-zag manner is termed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brownian-motion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brownian motion** is defined as the erratic or **uncontrolled movement of particles **in a fluid due to their constant collision with other molecules of fast-moving.
 
• The Brownian motion is also known as the **Brownian movement.**
 
• It was explained by **Robert Brown.**
 
• In water, This movement resembles the exact motion of **pollen grains.**
 
• The Brownian movement effect is seen in all types of **colloidal solutions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This phenomenon clearly explains the random motion of **Sol particles **and indicates that these are not static.
 
• The random movement of a particle is observed to be **stronger in a less viscous liquid, smaller-sized particles, and at a higher temperature.**
 
• **Tyndall effect i**s the scattering of light by colloid particles. It is similar to Rayleigh scattering.
 
• **Electrophoresis** is an electrokinetic process that separates charged particles in a fluid using a field of electrical charge.
 
• **Dialysis **is the process of removing excess water, solutes, and toxins from the blood in people whose kidneys can no longer perform these functions naturally.

questions.question: A metal is extracted from cinnabar ore by strong heating. What are alloys of this metal with other metals collectively known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amalgam**.__

__**Concept:**__

**Alloy:** An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal. 

**Mineral: **Minerals are **naturally occurring inorganic solids** with a crystalline structure and a definite range of chemical formulas.

**Ore: **Ores are **concentrations of minerals** in rock that are high enough to be **economically extracted for use.**

**__Explanation:__**

**Cinnabar:**

__
 
• It is bright red or brownish-red mineral formed of **mercuric sulfide **(mercury(II) sulfide).
 
• It is found close to areas of volcanic activity and hot springs.
 
• It is the **main commercial source of mercury**.
 
• **Chemical Formula: HgS.**

**Amalgam**

 
• It is an **alloy of mercury **and one or more other metals.
 
• It is **crystalline in structure,** except for those with a high mercury content, which is liquid.

So, **the metal extracted from cinnabar ore by strong heating is Mercury and the alloys of this metal with other metals are collectively known as amalgam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Nichrome**: It is an alloy of nickel, chromium, and iron** (Ni + Cr + Fe).**
 
• **Steel: ** It is an alloy of iron and carbon **(****Fe + C).**
 
• **German silver:** It is an alloy of** **copper, zinc, and nickel (**Cu + Zn + Ni).**

questions.question: Convex Mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in cars and motor-vehicles due to which of the following characteristic property?

options.text: It forms inverted image of the object
It forms real image of the object
It forms larger image of the object
It forms a smaller image as compared with the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It forms a smaller image as compared with the object**__.

__
 
• **A convex mirror,** also known as** a diverging mirror, is a mirror **in which the reflective surface **bulges toward the light source.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• A **convex mirror **reflects the light outwards and is therefore not used to focus light.
 
• Convex-mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in cars and motor-vehicles.
 
• This is because the image formed by the convex mirror is always erect, virtual and smaller than the object which helps drivers to see other vehicles coming up behind them.

questions.question: Which nervous system is responsible for carrying motor and sensory information?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Somatic.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Somatic nervous controls the **voluntary actions** in the body by **transmitting impulses** from **CNS to skeletal muscle cells**. It consists of the somatic nerves.
 
• The somatic nervous system is **responsible** for **carrying motor** and **sensory information**.
 
• It is made up of nerves that connect to the skin, sensory organs, and skeletal muscles.
 
• The **somatic** system is responsible for **all voluntary muscle movements** as well as for processing sensory information from external stimuli. (Hearing, touching, and sight).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The autonomic nervous system - **T**he nervous system that controls and regulates the internal organs without any conscious recognition or effort by the organism. 
 
• **Afferent** is responsible for transmitting messages from tissues and organs to the CNS.

questions.question:
In this reaction -

2Al + 6H⁺ → 2Al³⁺ + 3H₂ What is being oxidised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Oxidation **occurs when an atom, molecule, or ion** loses one or more electrons in a chemical reaction. **When oxidation occurs, the oxidation state of the chemical species increases.
 
• Oxidation doesn't necessarily involve oxygen.
 
• **Here Al has lost 3 electrons to become Al³⁺ **hence as per the above definition** Al has oxidized while H⁺ has reduced. **Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• The name aluminum is derived from the ancient name for alum (potassium aluminum sulfate), which was alumen (Latin, meaning bitter salt).
 
• Aluminum was the original name given to the element by Humphry Davy but others called it aluminum and that became the accepted name in Europe.
